stories.sourceTitle: FDA Approves First Treatment for Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9
supportingPassages: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Welgemda (ribitol), the first medicine for treating limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9), a rare inherited muscle disease, for adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg.
Welgemda is the first therapy approved for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
LGMD2I/R9 is caused by mutations in the FKRP gene, which disrupt a key biological process in muscle cells.
Personal income increased $201.8 billion (0.7 percent at a monthly rate) in October, according to estimates released today by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).
Disposable personal income (DPI)—personal income less personal current taxes—increased $200.5 billion (0.8 percent), and personal consumption expenditures (PCE) increased $63.8 billion (0.3 percent).
From the preceding month, the PCE price index for October increased 0.3 percent.

stories.sourceTitle: SHEIN to Pay $100 Million Over Allegations of Deceptive and Unfair Practices
supportingPassages: SHEIN will pay $100 million in consumer redress to settle Federal Trade Commission allegations that the fast-fashion retailer made it unreasonably difficult for consumers to resolve purchase issues, failed to keep its shipping promises, suppressed negative reviews and made deceptive supply chain and cotton-origin claims, all in violation of the law.

In a complaint, the FTC alleges that, through its practices, SHEIN violated Section 5 of the FTC Act, the Mail, Internet, or Telephone Order Merchandise Rule, and the Rule on the Use of Consumer Reviews and Testimonials.

The complaint alleges that SHEIN marketed fast, transparent and reliable shipping but tens of thousands of consumers reported that their orders arrived days, weeks or months late, while some consumers never received their orders at all.
